subtopics.title: The Table's Architecture — Atomic Number, Groups and Periods

questions.question: The modern periodic table orders the elements by:
options: Increasing atomic number — the proton count

questions.question: An element's period number equals:
options: Its proton count divided by two
The number of energy levels its electrons occupy
The number of neutrons in its nucleus

questions.question: Elements in the same group behave alike because they share:
options: The same number of valence electrons

questions.question: The configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p4 places the element at:
Relative to the staircase line, the three kingdoms sit:
options: Metals upper right, non-metals left, metalloids at the bottom
Metals to the left, non-metals to the upper right, metalloids along the line itself
Metals along the line, metalloids to the left

questions.question: The ion habits of the two sides are:
options: Metals gain electrons; non-metals lose them
Metals lose electrons to form cations; non-metals gain electrons to form anions

questions.question: Silicon runs the electronics industry because metalloids are:
options: Semiconductors — conducting between metal and insulator, and controllably so

questions.question: The strongly magnetic metals are:

subtopics.title: Trends Across and Down — Radius, Ionisation Energy, Electronegativity

questions.question: Atomic radius decreases across a period because:
options: Electrons are removed at each step
Added protons pull on the same outer level, reeling the shells inward

questions.question: Ionisation energy decreases down a group because the outer electron:
options: Sits further out and is screened by more inner electrons, so it leaves cheaply

questions.question: The strongest electron-puller in a bond — the most electronegative element — is:
options: Fluorine, top right of the trend

questions.question: The one picture holding all four trends is:
options: Across a period the nucleus wins; down a group distance and screening win
Trends run the same way in every direction
Electrons decide everything; protons decide nothing

subtopics.title: Group Portraits — Alkali Metals to Noble Gases

questions.question: The alkali metals are stored under oil because they:
options: Attack air and water on contact — one cheap valence electron makes them fiercely reactive

questions.question: Potassium reacts more violently with water than sodium because its outer electron:
options: Sits a level further out, better screened, and leaves even more easily

questions.question: Down the halogen family, reactivity:
options: Decreases — fluorine seizes electrons ferociously, iodine only mildly

questions.question: The noble gases are unreactive because they:
options: Have full outer levels — nothing to lose, nothing to gain

subtopics.title: The Street Map of the Elements

questions.question: In the street-map picture, your row tells you:
options: How many floors of electrons your house has

questions.question: The top floor matters most because:
options: The valence electrons there are the only ones other atoms ever meet

questions.question: An element whose configuration ends 2s1 has the address:
Walking across a row, the grip on outer electrons tightens because:
options: More pullers join the team while the rope stays the same length

questions.question: Walking down a column, the grip weakens because:
options: The rope lengthens with each new floor and inner floors muffle the pull
The team pulls in the wrong direction

questions.question: The corners of the table follow from the game:
options: Bottom left grips hardest; top right weakest
Top right — short rope, big team — pulls fiercest; bottom left — long rope, muffled — weakest
Only the middle of the table shows trends

questions.question: The alkali metals are the kid with one marble, meaning:
options: They hold one valence electron they shed at the slightest bump — the most reactive metals, forming plus-one ions

questions.question: The halogens' reactivity mirror says:
options: Both metals and non-metals strengthen downward
Giver families strengthen going down; collector families weaken going down
Reactivity never changes within a family

questions.question: Noble gases fill party balloons and glowing signs because:
options: They are the lightest elements known
They glow on their own in daylight
Their full outer levels make them react with essentially nobody
